h: Avraham's Ushpiza: "Then You Shall Delight upon Hashem"

p: בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (אֱמוֹר, זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קד, א):
In the holy Zohar (Emor, Zohar III 104a):
״אָז תִּתְעַנַּג עַל ה׳״ וְגוֹ׳ (יְשַׁעְיָה נח, יד).
'Then you shall delight in Hashem,' etc." (Yeshayah 58:14).
(סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת אַחֲרֵי, זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג עט, ב):
for children depend on the holy mazal, etc.;
and the upper tip of the yud
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (שָׁם סה, ב),
as stated in the holy Zohar (ibid. 65b);
of all hidden ones, which is called Ayin.
as stated in the holy Zohar
of the holy Atika shone forth
in His crowns, engraved and inscribed in the alef,
and the alef bored into the darkness
and shone to every side, etc.,
And it is stated in the holy Zohar
there is chessed and there is chessed, etc.;
the supernal chessed is 'above the heavens,' etc."
who merited recognizing the middah of Atika;
and this is what is said,
"And Avraham was old, coming with days" (Bereishis 24:1),
and it is stated in the holy Zohar
(חַיֵּי שָׂרָה, זֹהַר חֵלֶק א קכט, א):
that is, he was refined in all the middos
and this is why it says 'old,' precisely.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא פז, א):
And this is what the Gemara says (Bava Metzia 87a):
"Until Avraham there was no old age";
that is, there was no one
(בְּרֵאשִׁית, זֹהַר חֵלֶק א כו, א, סוֹף עַמּוּד א);
(Bereishis, Zohar I 26a, end of the amud);
for on Sukkos one also merits
as stated in Ra'aya Mehemna, Pinchas
which is a day of the souls
and not a day of the body,
as stated in the holy Zohar
(וַיַּקְהֵל, זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב רה, א, סוֹף עַמּוּד א).
(Vayakhel, Zohar II 205a, end of the amud).
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ בְּמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (סוּכָּה ב, א):
And as we have explained regarding what was taught (Sukkah 2a):
Now the phrase 'all seven days' is superfluous,
that the festival of Sukkos is seven days;
that in all the seven middos
and it is not written 'in six' —
one must leave the permanent dwelling
that is, to be like Shabbos,
which is a day of the souls
and not a day of the body at all,
as stated in the holy Zohar
And this is a dwelling for Hashem Yisbarach,
"And where is the place of My rest?" etc.;
"But to this one will I look,
to the poor and broken in spirit,
and this is expounded (beginning of Seder Eliyahu Rabbah)
as referring to the day of Shabbos.
And so on Sukkos the Torah said,
is called an 'inn' in the Gemara
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּגְּמָרָא מוֹעֵד קָטָן ט, ב);
(as written in the Gemara, Moed Katan 9b);
that it is a temporary dwelling,
then he becomes a dwelling for the Shechinah.
And this is what is said (Vayikra 23:43):
"So that your generations may know," etc.,
that this applies for all generations;
even after there will cease and be destroyed
the Beis HaMikdash and the Mishkan,
which are a dwelling for the Shechinah,
And this is what was said (Tanchuma Emor 22):
to make a sukkah for Me,
to repay Me My kindness, etc.,
as though you were doing kindness before Me, etc."
it likens the mitzvah of sukkah
to one who comes to pour a cup for his master.
And the point is: on Rosh Hashanah
there is the mitzvah of shofar,
so that they accept the yoke of His kingship
on Yom Kippur, the mitzvah of affliction;
and in a fast, the diminishing of my fat and blood
is as though I had offered it
"My offering, My bread for My fires."
And regarding sukkah, it is stated in the holy Zohar
קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא חָדֵי עִמֵּיהּ וְכוּלֵּי;
Kudsha Brich Hu rejoices with him, etc."
pouring a cup for his master,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
in the manner of what the holy Zohar says
is like pouring a cup for one's master.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 104a (Emor) — "Let a person not say, I will first eat and be satisfied and drink, and what remains I will give to the poor; rather, the first of all belongs to the guests. And if he gladdens the guests and satisfies them, the Holy One rejoices with him, and Avraham recites over him, 'Then you shall delight in Hashem' (Yeshayahu 58:14), and Yitzchak recites over him, 'No weapon formed against you shall succeed' (Yeshayahu 54:17). Rabbi Shimon said: That is what David the King said of him, for all the King's weapons and wars were entrusted into David's hands; but Yitzchak says, 'His seed shall be mighty in the land… wealth and riches are in his house' (Tehillim 112:2–3)."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 46 — “‘Then you shall delight upon (al) Hashem’ (Yeshayahu 58:14), as the holy Zohar says (end of Acharei) that ‘al Hashem’ is Atika, as it is written, ‘And Chanah prayed al Hashem,’ and ‘Cast your burden al Hashem’; that is, it is above the Name Havayah — the crown of the yud, for the Name Havayah includes the nine middos.” Connection: Rav Tzadok's other treatment of the same two Zohar passages, joining Avraham's “delight upon Hashem” to the level above the Name.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 79b (Acharei Mos) — "It is written of Chanah, 'She prayed upon (al) Hashem' — 'upon' precisely, because children depend on the holy Mazal." And: "'Cast your burden upon (al) Hashem' — 'upon' precisely, for sustenance depends on Mazal."

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 54a — “When the light of the Holy Ancient One shines in His engraved, inscribed crowns … the Alef pierces the darkness and shines to every side.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Pekudei 9 — “‘And what blessing is it that blesses this table that is set and delighted in properly? Then you shall delight in Hashem,’ for this is said in the verse about one who delights in Shabbos… ‘and you call Shabbos a delight… then you shall delight,’ that is, he merits the revelation of the aspect of Atika, which is called ‘al Hashem,’ above Hashem.” Connection: Both read “then (az) you shall delight in Hashem” as the revelation of Atika above the Name.

paragraphs.text: Zohar I 219a (Vayechi) — "'To behold the pleasantness of Hashem' (Tehillim 27:4) — this is the longing of the righteous… 'Then you shall delight al (above) Hashem' (Yeshayahu 58:14) — the pleasantness of Hashem that comes from the Holy Atika to these heavens. Fortunate is the portion of one who merits it; they are few."

paragraphs.text: Zohar I 129a (Chayei Sarah) — "When he grew old and entered the supernal levels as is fitting, as it is written, 'And Avraham was old,' then he 'came into days' — into those supernal days, the days known in the secret of faith; 'and Hashem blessed Avraham with everything (bakol)' — from where all blessings and all good issue."

paragraphs.text: Bava Metzia 87a — “Until Avraham there was no old age. One wishing to speak with Avraham would speak with Yitzchak; one wishing to speak with Yitzchak would speak with Avraham. Avraham came and asked for mercy, and old age came to be, as it says, 'Avraham was old, advanced in days.'” The Gemara explains the visible distinction of old age between father and son. Rav Tzadok reads this manifestation as the outward sign of Avraham's attainment of Atika; that mystical identification is his further interpretation.

paragraphs.text: Zohar I 26a (Bereishis) — "At that time it will be said of Moshe and Israel, 'Then you shall delight (tisaneg) upon Hashem' (Yeshayahu 58:14) — with oneg, which is ayin, Eden; nun, nahar (river); gimel, gan (garden)… and it will be turned for the Erev Rav, from oneg (delight) to nega (plague)."

paragraphs.text: Sukkah 2a — "Rava said: From here: 'In sukkos you shall dwell seven days' (Vayikra 23:42) — the Torah said: All seven days, leave your permanent dwelling and dwell in a temporary dwelling."

paragraphs.text: Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah 1 — "From here they said: a person should rise early on Shabbos and learn, go to the synagogue and the study hall, read in the Torah and learn in the Prophets, and afterward go home and eat and drink… for the Holy One has rest only with those who toil in Torah, as it says, '…but to this one I will look: to the poor and broken in spirit, who trembles at My word' (Yeshayahu 66:2)."

paragraphs.text: Tanchuma, Emor 22 — "The Holy One said to Israel: In this world I told you to make a sukkah, to repay Me for the kindness I did with you, as it says, 'In sukkos you shall dwell seven days, so that your generations may know that I made the Children of Israel dwell in sukkos' (Vayikra 23:42–43); and I regard it as though you were doing kindness before Me."

paragraphs.text: Sukkah 28b (Mishnah) — "All seven days a person makes his sukkah permanent and his house temporary. If rain fell, from when is it permitted to leave? From when the porridge would spoil. A parable: to what is this comparable? To a servant who came to pour a cup for his master, and he poured a pitcher on his face."

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah 16a — "Why did the Torah say to pour water on the festival? The Holy One said: Pour water before Me on the festival, so that the rains of the year be blessed for you. And say before Me on Rosh Hashanah Malchiyos, Zichronos and Shofaros: Malchiyos — so that you crown Me King over you; Zichronos — so that your remembrance rise before Me for good; and with what? With the shofar."

paragraphs.text: Berachos 17a — "When Rav Sheshes sat in a fast, after praying he would say: Master of the worlds, it is revealed before You that when the Beis HaMikdash stood, a person who sinned brought an offering, and only its fat and blood were offered, and he was atoned. Now I have sat in a fast and my fat and blood have diminished; may it be Your will that my diminished fat and blood be as though I had offered them before You on the altar."
